topic: Which Grand Slam is still played on grass? (Wimbledon — London SW19, since 1877)
policy_note: Every spoken or shown fact → a claim with ≥ 2 independent publishers; core claims need a primary/scholarly source.

wimbledon_history_1870s.title: History — 1870s: The First Championships
wimbledon_history_1870s.notes: first Championship meeting 1877 at the All England Croquet and Lawn Tennis Club, Worple Road, Wimbledon; one event (gentlemen's singles) won by Spencer Gore; total attendance for the final was 200; club founded for croquet 1868, one lawn given to lawn tennis 1875

wimbledon_history.title: History — decade overview
wimbledon_history.notes: inaugural Championships: entry of 22 men attracted by an announcement in The Field; crowd of 200 watch Spencer Gore become the first Champion; 1922 move from Worple Road to Church Road

wiki_wimbledon.title: Wimbledon Championships
wiki_wimbledon.notes: held since 1877 on outdoor grass; the only major still played on grass; US Open abandoned grass in 1975 (green clay), Australian Open in 1988 (hard); courts 100% perennial ryegrass since 2001 (70/30 rye/fescue before)

wiki_us_open.title: US Open (tennis)
wiki_us_open.notes: first held 1881 on grass at Newport; from 1975 played on clay instead of grass; since 1978 acrylic hard courts at Flushing Meadows

wiki_australian_open.title: Australian Open
wiki_australian_open.notes: formerly on grass; switched to hard court (Rebound Ace) in 1988 with the move to Flinders Park

wiki_grass_court.title: Grass court
wiki_grass_court.notes: since 1988 Wimbledon is the only Grand Slam on grass; US Open last on grass 1974 (clay 1975–77); Australian Open last on grass January 1987

guardian_2025.title: 'It makes water wetter': How Wimbledon keeps grass green in soaring temperatures
guardian_2025.notes: Neil Stubley, head of courts and horticulture: mowers set each morning, grass tailored to a precise 8mm; 20 full-time grounds staff

guardian_2012.title: Wimbledon 2012: Centre Court's grass whisperer faces final challenge
guardian_2012.notes: head groundsman Eddie Seaward: the lawn is shaved to an 8mm stubble

britannica_us_open.title: U.S. Open (tennis)
britannica_us_open.notes: played on grass 1881–1974, clay 1975–1977, hard courts since 1978 (Flushing Meadows); author Chris Evert

tennis365_us_open.title: US Open facts and figures: from the various surfaces to the trophies
tennis365_us_open.notes: grass 1881–1974, clay 1975–1977, hard from 1978; Connors won on all three

claims.text: Wimbledon is the only Grand Slam still played on grass; The Championships have been held at Wimbledon, south-west London (SW19), since 1877.
vo: which grand slam is still played on grass
it's wimbledon, in south-west london, on grass since eighteen seventy-seven

claims.text: The first Championships (1877, Worple Road) had an entry of 22 men, a single event (gentlemen's singles, won by Spencer Gore) and a final watched by 200 people.
vo: first championships: twenty-two men, one event, two hundred watching

claims.text: The US Open left grass after 1974 (clay from 1975, hard courts from 1978); the Australian Open moved from grass to hard courts in 1988 (last grass edition January 1987).
vo: the us open left grass in nineteen seventy-five, australia in nineteen eighty-eight

claims.text: Wimbledon's courts have been sown with 100% perennial ryegrass since 2001 and are cut to 8 mm for The Championships.
vo: the courts: pure ryegrass, cut to eight millimetres

myths.myth: All four Slams were once on grass.
myths.reality: The French Open has been on clay; the US and Australian Opens were on grass until 1974 and 1987.

myths.myth: Wimbledon's grass is a traditional seed mix.
myths.reality: Since 2001 the courts are 100% perennial ryegrass, chosen for durability.
